body:
A follow-up to #5861.

Instructions, macOS / Linux GCC 13 / Linux Clang 18:

| commit | change |
|---|---|
| Resume patch pointers from the previous operation and read operation members in one pass | patch canada 85.8 -> 67.7M / 67.4 -> 42.6M / 70.0 -> 43.6M |
| Scan reference tokens and array indices in place in `resolve_plain()` | patch -10 % (Linux) |
| Skip the token copy for array indices and the prefix look-up for a first child 0 in `unflatten()` | canada -14 ... -16 % |
| Reserve the storage of an `ordered_json` in `flatten()` once | citm -37 %, twitter -34 % |
| Add the members of a diff operation without looking them up | -4 % / -1 % / -9 % |
| Keep the target values of a diffed object of up to 16 members on the stack | citm -7 % |
| Write the path of an array element in `flatten()` with a single resize | canada -4.3 % |
| Search once for a new object member in `unflatten()` and `j[json_pointer]` | twitter -6 % / -13 % |
| Reserve room for two elements in the arrays `unflatten()` creates | canada -13 % |

The first commit also adds an `is_dash()` helper. GCC turned `reference_token == "-"` into a `strlen` and `memcmp` call: `contains()` was 15 % slower before the helper and is now unchanged.

## Numbers

macOS timing vs develop:

| benchmark | ratio |
|---|---|
| FlattenOrdered | 0.63 |
| Patch | 0.82 |
| Unflatten | 0.85 |
| Diff | 0.91 |

No benchmark is slower than +0.6 % (noise).

## Validation

- Differential check against develop, byte-identical, in plain, `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` and `JSON_DIAGNOSTIC_POSITIONS` builds:
  - the corpus, as `json` and `ordered_json`;
  - 60,000 random rounds of documents, patches and pointers, valid and invalid;
  - exception ids and messages.
- 46 unit test runs with ASan/UBSan, in C++11 and C++20.
- All commits build on their own, and each commit's `single_include` is a fresh `make amalgamate`.

## Public API

No breaking changes.

Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.
